angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 788,450 km at 42.25 pc = 0.25 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 23.6673 +/- 0.0251 mas (same row, RUWE 0.98): 42.25 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 1.133 (1.111 to 1.156) from Gaia DR3 FLAME (Creevey et al. 2023, A&A 674, A26; astrophysical_parameters of the same source): 788,450 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.984 (0.944 to 1.024) from Gaia DR3 FLAME (Creevey et al. 2023, A&A 674, A26; astrophysical_parameters of the same source); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 5777 +/- 1.9 K from Andrae et al. (2023), A&A 674, A27 (Gaia DR3 GSP-Phot), astrophysical_parameters of Gaia DR3 4988158666636598272: teff_gspphot 5776.7295 K (16th-84th percentiles 5775.3755-5779.2227), the temperature FLAME used (https://doi.org/10.1051/0004-6361/202243462). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Andrae et al. (2023), A&A 674, A27 (Gaia DR3 GSP-Phot), astrophysical_parameters of Gaia DR3 4988158666636598272: teff_gspphot 5776.7295 K (16th-84th percentiles 5775.3755-5779.2227), the temperature FLAME used (https://doi.org/10.1051/0004-6361/202243462)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/nenque.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.322, rounded to two decimals
